brief.headline: Aluminium fell for a second straight session and underperformed the base-metal complex again, as a reported US-Iran ceasefire and an Iran-Oman safe-corridor plan for the Strait of Hormuz began deflating the geopolitical risk premium that has supported the metal since March.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: the LME aluminium cash official settled at $3,188.00 on 25-August, down $27.50 (-0.85%), and three-month at $3,206.50, down $28.50 (-0.88%). Copper, zinc and lead all settled higher on the same session; aluminium and nickel fell. Exchange stock ticked down 100 tonnes to 246,825, the first movement in the warehouse line since 17-August and far too small to call a draw.

WHY IT MOVED: the biggest change is geopolitical, not industrial. Reports circulated of a US-Iran ceasefire agreement - not confirmed by either government - and Iran and Oman issued a joint statement planning a mutually agreed safe maritime corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, roughly seven nautical miles wide, described as temporary with a permanent route to be negotiated within 30 to 60 days. Iran's deputy foreign minister was explicit that the memorandum does NOT mean the strait reopens on 26-August. A risk premium that took months to build is being priced out faster than the physical route is actually reopening.

THE OTHER SIDE OF THE LEDGER: supply keeps returning. Outside China, daily average primary output is expected to keep rebounding on new capacity commissioning and restarts. Against that, Chinese aluminium ingot social inventory kept drawing - 860,000 tonnes on 24-August, down 26,000 tonnes week on week - which is the clearest remaining bull support. Chinese warehouses are emptying while LME warehouses have gone flat, and those two signals genuinely disagree.

WHAT TO WATCH: whether the $3,183.00 three-month low of 20-August holds, because it is only $23.50 below today's forward and it is the last support before the $3,159.50 level that would say this correction is deeper than a normal pullback. Beyond the tape: confirmation or denial of the ceasefire by either government, the permanent Hormuz route talks inside the stated 30-60 day window, and the opening of Q4 Japanese premium negotiations, conventionally in early September.

lme.commentary: THE FIFTEEN-SESSION WINDOW NOW RUNS 05-AUGUST TO 25-AUGUST AND IT ROLLED THIS RUN: the 25-August session was appended and 04-August dropped, so the length is held at fifteen. THE SHAPE IS A CLEAN LOWER-HIGH SEQUENCE AND IT SHOULD BE READ AS ONE. Cash peaked at $3,373.00 on 11-August, then $3,272.00 on 17-August, then $3,227.00 on 21-August, and today $3,188.00. Each rally has failed lower than the last, and the $3,182.00 cash low of 20-August is now only $6.00 below today's print. THE STOCK LINE TELLS THE STRUCTURAL STORY: 259,400 tonnes at the start of this window, 246,925 by 17-August, and 246,825 today - which is to say the entire drawdown in this window happened in its first eight sessions and the last seven have moved a net 100 tonnes. THE DESTOCKING ENGINE THAT CARRIED PRICE THROUGH JUNE AND JULY HAS IDLED, AND THAT IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THIS CHART. The curve overlay adds the third dimension: cash and three-month were on top of each other at $3,272.00 on 17-August, and every session since has printed a contango. A market that stops paying for prompt metal at the same moment its warehouse draw stops is telling a consistent story about the front end, and that story is looser rather than tighter. COUNTERWEIGHT, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED: none of this is a collapse. The window's low is $3,182.00, the August month-to-date cash average is $3,254.74, and price is still roughly 22% above the same point a year ago on the Trading Economics reference series. This is a market losing a risk premium, not one losing a floor. Source: Westmetall LME official settlements and stocks, 25-Aug-2026 board.

drivers.text: The Q4 Japanese scenario range is LOWERED this run, and the reason is the Hormuz corridor statement rather than anything in the tape — The pending Q4-2026 range on this board is moved to $300-390/t from $305-395/t, and the change is stated rather than slipped in. The logic is specific: the Q3 settlement of $395/t was the highest Main Japanese Port premium in roughly a decade and it was struck while the Strait of Hormuz was closed and Gulf supply into Asia was genuinely impaired. On 26-August Iran and Oman issued a joint statement planning a mutually agreed safe maritime corridor through the strait, described by Iran's deputy foreign minister as a temporary ~7-nautical-mile two-way lane with a permanent route to be negotiated in 30 to 60 days. THE STRAIT HAS NOT REOPENED AND THE SAME OFFICIAL SAID EXPLICITLY THAT IT DOES NOT REOPEN ON 26-AUGUST, so this is de-escalation in principle, not restored logistics. But Q4 negotiations conventionally open in early September, inside the very 30-60 day window in which the permanent route is to be settled, and buyers will negotiate against that. The upper bound is held near the Q3 settlement because the strait is still closed today; the lower bound is cut because the CIF Japan spot row is already $25/t BELOW the Q3 benchmark, which is the physical market declining to pay the benchmark. THIS IS A SCENARIO RANGE, NOT AN ASSESSMENT, AND IT IS LABELLED AS ONE.
drivers.source: SMM Aluminum Morning Meeting Minutes, 26-Aug-2026 - Iran-Oman safe maritime corridor plan; strait not reopening on 26-August

drivers.text: Roughly 76% of the US duty-paid premium is tariff rather than scarcity - and the tariff itself is now the thing that is moving — At the 50% Section 232 rate on wholly-aluminium articles, the tariff leg on today's $3,188.00 cash price is about $1,594.00/t inside a US Midwest duty-paid premium of $2,094/t, leaving roughly $500/t of genuine freight, financing and regional scarcity. Two mechanical points follow and both matter for anyone reading this premium as a demand signal. FIRST, the tariff leg is a percentage of the metal price, so it fell $13.75 today purely because cash fell $27.50 - the premium's largest component moves with the LME whether or not anything happens in the US physical market. SECOND, and far larger: the September premium slumped 8.2% to 95 cents a pound on 20-August and October and November contracts fell more than 12%, on reports that the United States is set to cut tariffs on Canadian metal to 25% from 50% under a tentative deal whose details are unfinalised and which is not expected to apply across the board. NO PROCLAMATION HAS BEEN PUBLISHED, so the 50% rate is retained here; but a premium that is three-quarters policy will re-rate on a signature, not on a supply-demand balance.
drivers.source: MINING.COM / Bloomberg - Aluminum premium slips as US set to cut tariffs on Canada metal, 20-Aug-2026 (September MW premium -8.2% to 95c/lb; Oct-Nov contracts -12%)

drivers.text: The Asian physical signal is unchanged and still soft - the off-season has not handed over to the peak season — SMM's 26-August aluminium morning meeting states that the traditional consumption off-season is nearing its end but that the transition period between off-season and peak season HAS NOT YET APPEARED, with downstream processing operating rates under pressure overall. Export demand is pulling back month on month as the SHFE/LME ratio repairs and orders on hand are digested, though July aluminium stranded wire exports of 102,800 tonnes far exceeded expectations and SMM describes the resilience as still present. THE OFFSET IS REAL AND IS NOT BURIED: Chinese aluminium ingot social inventory in major consumption regions drew to 860,000 tonnes on Monday 24-August, down 15,000 tonnes from the prior Thursday and 26,000 tonnes week on week. Physical premiums are ultimately paid out of downstream margin, and a market whose fabricators are running below capacity while its ingot stocks draw is sending two signals that do not resolve into one number.
drivers.source: SMM Aluminum Morning Meeting Minutes, 26-Aug-2026 - off-season to peak-season transition not yet appeared; ingot social inventory 860 kt on 24-Aug

drivers.text: Freight is still the quiet structural cost inside every delivered premium, and no newer print was published — The Baltic Dry Index stands at 2,882 points on its 24-August print, up 41 points (+1.44%) on the session - a third consecutive gain and the highest since 12-August, with Capesize at 4,643 (+2.0%), Panamax 2,131 (+1.3%) and Supramax 1,641 (+0.1%). NO 25-AUGUST OR 26-AUGUST PRINT HAD BEEN PUBLISHED AT THIS COMPILE, so the row is carried at its 24-August date rather than rolled forward. Capesize is the bauxite and alumina vessel class and it is leading, which is the part that matters for a smelter cost basket: Guinea-to-China freight running around $35-38/t against delivered ore of $70-74/t means ocean freight is approaching half the delivered cost of the ore. Every delivered premium on this page - CIF Japan, EDU Rotterdam, US Midwest - carries a freight leg, and that leg has been inflating quietly while the tariff and geopolitical legs took the headlines. IF THE HORMUZ CORRIDOR ACTUALLY OPENS, war-risk and routing surcharges should fall; BASE FREIGHT IS A SEPARATE AND STICKIER PROBLEM AND WILL NOT FALL WITH IT.
drivers.source: Trading Economics - Baltic Dry Index, 24-Aug-2026 print (BDI 2,882, +1.44%; Capesize 4,643); no 25/26-Aug print published at compile time

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THE MOST MATERIAL CHANGE ON THIS ENTIRE BOARD, AND THE TREND FLAG IS DELIBERATELY MOVED FROM UP TO DOWN FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE THE CLOSURE BEGAN. Per SMM's 26-August aluminium morning meeting: Iran and Oman issued a JOINT STATEMENT planning a mutually agreed safe maritime corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, with inbound and outbound Persian Gulf traffic routed through Iranian and Omani waters respectively - described by Iran's deputy foreign minister Gharibabadi as a 'two-way highway' about SEVEN NAUTICAL MILES wide. Separately, reports circulated of a US-Iran ceasefire agreement including freedom of navigation and resumed negotiations on the Islamabad Memorandum, and the US President posted that all mines in the international waters of the strait have been cleared or detonated, with a warning that any vessel laying new mines will be destroyed immediately. US diplomatic missions in the region may begin allowing diplomats to return as early as this week. NOW THE THREE QUALIFICATIONS THAT KEEP THIS HONEST, AND THEY ARE NOT SMALL. FIRST, NEITHER GOVERNMENT HAS CONFIRMED THE CEASEFIRE. SECOND, Gharibabadi stated EXPLICITLY that the memorandum does NOT mean the strait resumes opening from 26-August. THIRD, the corridor is described as TEMPORARY, with a permanent route to be negotiated within 30 to 60 days. So the correct label is de-escalation in principle, not restored logistics in fact - and the price is already trading the principle. The trend flag reads DOWN because the direction of travel on this risk has genuinely reversed, not because the strait is open. It is not.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: CARRIED, WITH THE DIRECTION UNCHANGED AND REINFORCED BY THE HORMUZ NEWS. Suez transits have been recovering toward a two-year high as Red Sea routing risk normalises, which shortens Asia-Europe voyage distances and releases vessel capacity back into the global pool. If the Hormuz corridor plan holds, the two chokepoints normalise together and the freight-length premium built into Asia-Europe and Gulf-Asia aluminium and alumina routes compresses from both ends at once. That would be a genuine structural easing of delivered cost - and it is a conditional statement, not a forecast.

logistics.note: HELD AT ITS 22-JULY MARK BECAUSE NO NEWER PUBLIC QUOTE WAS RETRIEVABLE, AND THE TREND IS MOVED FROM UP TO FLAT RATHER THAN TO DOWN. The reasoning is deliberately conservative: war-risk premia are quoted voyage by voyage in a private market and they reprice on WRITTEN, CONFIRMED changes in the risk environment - a signed ceasefire, a formal reopening notice, a change in the listed war-risk area - not on unconfirmed reports and a temporary corridor memorandum. THE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL IS CLEARLY DOWN AND IS SAID SO HERE, but marking the row down before a confirmed repricing would be forecasting the insurance market rather than reporting it. At 7.5-10% of hull value this remains one of the largest single distortions in delivered Gulf metal economics, and its unwind - if it comes - is worth more to regional delivered costs than any of the price moves on this page.

THE IMPORTANT DISTINCTION AGAINST TODAY'S HORMUZ NEWS: chokepoint risk and base dry-bulk freight are different things. A reopened strait removes war-risk surcharges and routing detours; it does not lower Capesize rates, which are set by vessel supply, iron ore and coal demand and Chinese restocking. Freight is the stickier of the two costs and it is still rising.

events.event: NALCO INAUGURATED A 50 kg/day PILOT PLANT AT ITS BHUBANESWAR
events.note: NALCO INAUGURATED A 50 kg/day PILOT PLANT AT ITS BHUBANESWAR RESEARCH CENTRE TO RECOVER VALUE FROM BITUMINOUS COAL FLY ASH - alumina, calcium silicate, quartz residue and an iron hydroxide residue enriched in rare earths including scandium - developed with CSIR-IMMT and KIIT. PILOT SCALE, NOT COMMERCIAL SCALE: 50 kg/day is a laboratory demonstration and no economics have been published. events.note: COPPER IS THE COMPLEX'S TIGHT METAL AND IT IS PULLING AWAY FROM ALUMINIUM. Copper cash settled $14,425.00 on 25-August against a $14,298.00 three-month, a BACKWARDATION of $127.00 widened from $99.00, with stock down 1,525 tonnes to 238,725. Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it. A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. IT IS A SMALL COMPANY AND ONE QUARTER, SO IT IS WEIGHTED ACCORDINGLY: it is evidence that extrusion demand outside China is holding, not evidence that the global peak season has arrived.

earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: SWUNG BACK TO PROFIT ON THE PRICE CYCLE, WITH TEXTBOOK OPERATING LEVERAGE. Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. Total sales cost rose 3.3% to US$6.31bn, attributed to higher energy costs. REVENUE UP A TENTH AGAINST EBITDA UP NEARLY TWO-THIRDS IS THE SAME OPERATING-LEVERAGE SIGNATURE EVERY OTHER PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL HAS REPORTED FOR THE FIRST HALF, and it confirms the pattern extends beyond Western and Gulf smelters. The cost line is the part worth noting rather than the profit line: sales cost rose only 3.3% while revenue rose 10.9%, so the margin expansion came from price rather than from cost deflation, and the company specifically attributed what cost inflation there was to ENERGY. That is consistent with the power and carbon risk carried on the input basket. The half captured aluminium reaching four-year highs before the retreat now visible on this board, so it is a backward-looking confirmation of the cycle rather than a forward signal.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided hot metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter currently at about 18% of capacity. THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. Iran and Oman announced a plan for a mutually agreed safe maritime corridor roughly seven nautical miles wide, described as TEMPORARY with a permanent route to be negotiated in 30 to 60 days; a US-Iran ceasefire including freedom of navigation is reported but UNCONFIRMED by either government; and Iran's deputy foreign minister stated EXPLICITLY that the memorandum does not mean the strait reopens on 26-August. A corridor that is planned, temporary and not yet operating is not a restored trade route, and re-drawing the flow map on an announcement rather than on transits would be exactly the kind of premature reclassification this map is designed to avoid. THE TRIGGER FOR CHANGING THESE ENTRIES IS STATED SO IT CAN BE HELD TO: confirmed resumption of commercial transits, or a permanent-route agreement, whichever comes first. The second live trigger on this map is unrelated and is a US proclamation altering the Canadian tariff rate, which would change the North American corridor economics rather than the Gulf ones.

catalysts.text: THE NEXT LME OFFICIAL, AND THE NARROWEST TEST THIS BOARD HAS SET IN WEEKS. The three-month official of $3,206.50 sits just $23.50 above the $3,183.00 low of 20-August and $47.00 above the $3,159.50 invalidation. Hold $3,183.00 and the two-day sell-off is a correction inside the summer uptrend that found support exactly where it should have. Lose it and the next argument is $3,159.50, below which the wave count on this board says the correction is deeper than a normal second wave. Watch the spread alongside the price: a contango that WIDENS on a further fall would confirm the front end is loosening, while a further narrowing would repeat today's mildly constructive divergence.

CONFIRMATION OR DENIAL OF THE REPORTED US-IRAN CEASEFIRE. Reports describe an agreement including freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and resumed negotiations on the Islamabad Memorandum, expected to be officially announced in coming days. NEITHER GOVERNMENT HAS CONFIRMED IT. A confirmed ceasefire accelerates the risk-premium unwind already visible in both aluminium and crude; a public denial or a breakdown would reprice it back up sharply, because the market has already started trading the announcement. Secondary tells: whether US diplomatic missions in the region actually begin allowing diplomats to return this week, as reported.

THE PERMANENT HORMUZ ROUTE NEGOTIATION. Iran's deputy foreign minister put an explicit 30-to-60-day window on converting the temporary Iran-Oman corridor into a permanent route, and was equally explicit that the memorandum does not mean the strait reopens on 26-August. THE OBSERVABLE MILESTONE IS TRANSITS, NOT STATEMENTS: commercial vessel movements through the corridor, war-risk insurance repricing off the 7.5-10% of hull value carried on this board, and the withdrawal of force-majeure declarations by Gulf producers would each be harder evidence than any communique.

Q4-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS OPEN, AND THEY OPEN INTO A CHANGED WORLD. Q3 settled at $395/t CIF Japan - the highest Main Japanese Port premium in roughly a decade - and it was struck while the strait was closed. Spot is carried at $370/t, $25/t BELOW the benchmark, which is the physical market already declining to pay it. The scenario range on this board was lowered to $300-390/t this run on the corridor announcement. The negotiation window overlaps the 30-60 day permanent-route window, so buyers will be negotiating against a live de-escalation process.

A US PROCLAMATION ON CANADIAN METAL TARIFFS. Reporting indicates rates on some Canadian products could fall to 25% from 50% under a tentative deal that is unfinalised and not expected to apply across the board. The market has already moved: the September Midwest premium fell 8.2% to 95 cents a pound and October-November contracts fell more than 12%. Because roughly 76% of the US duty-paid premium is tariff at the current rate and price, the publication of a proclamation would re-rate the largest regional premium on this board in a single step.

CHINESE ALUMINIUM INGOT SOCIAL INVENTORY. This is now the single most important recurring datapoint on the bull side of the page and the only one still moving in the bulls' favour. SMM put major-region inventory at 860,000 tonnes on Monday 24-August, down 15,000 tonnes from the prior Thursday and 26,000 tonnes week on week. If Chinese destocking stalls while the LME line stays flat, the last tightness argument on this board goes with it.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - STILL THE DOMINANT RISK ON THIS BOARD AND NOW WITH ONE MORE NAMED ASSET BEHIND IT. SMM's 26-August daily repeats the aggregate: outside China, driven by new capacity commissioning and production resumptions, daily average production is expected to CONTINUE rebounding. The asset-level schedule beneath that sentence is EGA restoring Al Taweelah from ~18% of capacity toward pre-war output in Q1-2027, Century Aluminum holding 2026 guidance at 630 kt while ramping idled capacity in South Carolina and Iceland, and Alcoa's Portland and San Ciprian restarts already complete. This is not a forecast of supply; it is a published timetable of it.

THE STOCK DRAW HAS STOPPED AND EIGHT SESSIONS NOW CONFIRM IT. LME aluminium stock went from 303,675 tonnes at end-June to 246,925 by 17-August - a 56,750 tonne draw - and has since moved a NET 100 TONNES, ticking to 246,825 on 25-August. The 100-tonne move is directionally a draw and is honestly the first movement in over a week, but it is 0.04% of the total and about forty minutes of global output. The destocking engine that carried price through June and July has idled, and a market that stops drawing while its curve sits in contango for seven straight sessions has lost the tightness argument at the front end.

THE HORMUZ RISK PREMIUM UNWINDS FASTER THAN THE PHYSICAL ROUTE ACTUALLY REOPENS - TREND MOVED FROM UP TO DOWN THIS RUN, THE FIRST SUCH CHANGE SINCE THE CLOSURE BEGAN, AND IT IS A DELIBERATE CALL. Iran and Oman issued a joint statement planning a mutually agreed safe maritime corridor through the strait, described by Iran's deputy foreign minister as a temporary ~7-nautical-mile two-way lane with a permanent route to be negotiated in 30-60 days; a US-Iran ceasefire including freedom of navigation is reported but UNCONFIRMED by either government; and the US President stated mines in international waters have been cleared. THE SAME IRANIAN OFFICIAL SAID EXPLICITLY THE STRAIT DOES NOT REOPEN ON 26-AUGUST. The risk is now asymmetric in the other direction: the premium is being priced out on an announcement, so a breakdown in the talks would reprice it back UP violently. The trend flag reads down because the direction of travel has genuinely reversed - not because the strait is open. It is not.

PHYSICAL DEMAND FAILS TO SHOW UP FOR THE PEAK SEASON. SMM's 26-August daily states the traditional off-season is nearing its end but the transition to peak season HAS NOT YET APPEARED, with downstream processing operating rates under pressure overall, and export demand pulling back month on month as the SHFE/LME ratio repairs and orders on hand are digested. Secondary alloy corroborates it: SMM ADC12 flat at 23,900 yuan/t with demand showing no significant improvement and price rises lacking transaction support. The offset is the ingot destocking, and the two signals have now disagreed for several weeks running.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. Trend held at DOWN because the unwind is visibly happening rather than pending, which reduces the residual risk. The clearest evidence is in the adjacent market: SHFE alumina 2610 fell 0.74% on 25-August on volume UP 58,743 lots while open interest FELL 13,903 - rising volume on falling open interest is position closing, not fresh shorting, and SMM reads it as profit-taking after the rebound. In aluminium itself, two consecutive sessions of underperformance against a rising complex on a firming dollar has the same signature.

AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK RE-EMERGES. Trend held at DOWN and the evidence got stronger this run. China alumina spot is expected at 2,550-2,650 yuan/t and grinding lower; national capacity utilisation rose 1.81 percentage points week on week to 82.79% on roughly 99.4 Mt/yr of operating capacity; traders' inventories built 73,000 tonnes to 6.565 Mt; and SHFE alumina 2610 closed down 0.74%. Caustic soda, the second-largest refinery consumable, is also lower at its last dated mark. The residual risk is seaborne rather than Chinese - SMM notes overseas prices rising on Middle East bagged-alumina demand and tight Indonesian bauxite, without publishing a figure.

SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE. TREND MOVED FROM UP TO FLAT-TO-DOWN THIS RUN AND IS SET TO DOWN, ON TWO SESSIONS OF CRUDE WEAKNESS. Brent fell 1.16% to $91.10 on 25-August after falling 2.57% on 24-August, with WTI at $83.88 (-1.33%); petroleum coke is a refinery co-product loosely tethered to the crude complex and the carbon re-inflation thesis on this board has leaned on crude strength as its driver. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION: it has NOT yet shown up in any published coke, pitch or anode mark - no CPC, green coke, CTP or prebaked anode figure newer than mid-August could be publicly retrieved this run - and European gas rose 0.30% while crude fell, so the energy complex is not easing uniformly.

US TRADE POLICY MOVES THE US DUTY-PAID PREMIUM - AND IT IS MOVING NOW RATHER THAN PENDING. The September US Midwest premium slumped 8.2% to 95 cents a pound on 20-August and October-November contracts fell more than 12%, on reports the United States is set to cut tariffs on Canadian metal to 25% from 50% under a tentative deal whose details are unfinalised and which is not expected to apply across the board. NO PROCLAMATION HAS BEEN PUBLISHED. At the 50% rate on today's $3,188 cash price the tariff leg is about $1,594/t of a $2,094/t duty-paid premium - roughly 76%. A premium that is three-quarters policy re-rates on a signature, and the risk is live in both directions until one is published.

FREIGHT AND DELIVERED-COST INFLATION INSIDE EVERY REGIONAL PREMIUM. The Baltic Dry stands at 2,882 on its 24-August print, up 1.44% and a third consecutive gain, Capesize-led at 4,643 (+2.0%); no 25 or 26-August print had been published at this compile. Guinea-to-China freight at roughly $35-38/t against delivered ore of $70-74/t means ocean freight is approaching half the delivered cost of the ore. THE POINT THAT MATTERS AGAINST TODAY'S NEWS: a reopened strait removes war-risk surcharges and routing detours but does NOT lower Capesize rates, which are set by vessel supply and bulk demand. Freight is the stickier of the two costs and it is still rising.

CARBON BORDER POLICY AND CERTIFICATION BECOME CONDITIONS OF MARKET ACCESS RATHER THAN DIFFERENTIATORS. Hindalco's Baphlimali mine became India's first ASI-certified bauxite operation under Performance Standard V3.1, extending a certified chain into roughly 2.67 Mt/yr of alumina and taking the group to eleven certified sites. Read alongside the EU's carbon border mechanism and the growing low-carbon premium channels, certification is migrating from a marketing claim to an entry requirement for the highest-value European and downstream channels. This is a slow risk with a long fuse and it is carried for that reason.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
